source.author: verg
source.text: Vinxerat et post terga manus, quos mitteret umbris inferias, caeso sparsuros sanguine flammas, indutosque iubet truncos hostilibus armis ipsos ferre duces inimicaque nomina figi.
source.text_original: Vinxerat et post terga manus, quos mitteret umbris / inferias, caeso sparsuros sanguine flammas, / indutosque iubet truncos hostilibus armis / ipsos ferre duces inimicaque nomina figi.
source.text_english: He had also bound their hands behind their backs, those he would send as offerings to the shades, to sprinkle the flames with their slaughtered blood, and he orders the trunks, clad in the weapons of their foes, to be carried by the leaders themselves and the hostile names to be fixed upon them.

reuse.text_english: He had bound his hands behind his back as well, so that, to send him as an offering to the shades, he might sprinkle the flames with the blood of the slain.
